name: Cameroonian Ndolé
description: Ndolé is Cameroon's national dish, and its name literally comes from the real bitter leaf (Vernonia amygdalina) at its center - traditionally boiled and rinsed two or three times specifically to soften its sharp bitterness while deliberately leaving some behind, since that residual bitter edge against the sweet peanut sauce is the entire point of the dish. Bitter leaf isn't a distinct item here, so spinach stands in for the greenery, but spinach has no bitterness at all to begin with, so this version is honestly missing the exact quality the dish is named for, not just a minor substitution.

name: Cameroonian Poulet DG
description: Poulet DG, meaning 'director general chicken', is a beloved Cameroonian dish combining fried chicken with plantain and vegetables, its name reflecting its status as a special-occasion favorite.
steps_detailed: Brown the chicken, 8-9 minutes, then set aside.
Fry the plantain slices, 3-4 minutes per side, until caramelized, then set aside.
Cook the bell pepper, carrot, and tomatoes 8-10 minutes.
Combine the chicken and plantain with the vegetables and warm through together.

name: Cameroonian Achu
description: Achu, cocoyam pounded into a smooth, stretchy mash and served with a distinctive yellow soup, is a genuine specialty of Cameroon's Northwest Region - real cocoyam isn't a distinct item here, so yam stands in for a similar starchy, pounded texture, though cocoyam's real flavor is honestly milder and starchier than yam's.

name: Cameroonian Egusi Soup
description: Egusi soup, thickened with real ground melon seeds, is shared with Nigeria and found throughout much of Central and West Africa, real technique frying the egusi paste in spoonfuls to build its characteristic lumpy texture.
steps_detailed: Brown the beef, 6-7 minutes.
Mix the egusi with water into a paste and fry spoonfuls in the palm oil until slightly golden, 5-6 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and beef, and simmer 10-12 minutes.
Stir in the spinach in the last 3 minutes.

name: Cameroonian Bongo Tchobi
description: Bongo tchobi, a dark, smoky black soup made with roasted seeds and spices, a genuine specialty of Cameroon's coastal Sawa people, real depth coming from deeply toasting the ground peanuts until nearly black.

ingredients_full.ingredient: Peanuts, all types, dry-roasted, with salt

Add the fish and simmer 10-12 minutes until just cooked through.
